text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Denmark's centre-left government agreed with the Socialist People's Party and the Unity list on granting 250 million for the environment in the 1997 state budget. In the leftist parties will support a rise in net income taxes.
--- Nearly 50 percent of all Danish companies will have moved production abroad at the beginning of the new century a new trade ministry report shows.
--- A new price war on mobile telephones is on its way with telecommunication companies Sonofon and Tele Danmark starting new sales campaigns next week.
--- Medical company Loevens Kemiske Fabrik and US medical company Cephalon are now cooperating on research on new remedies against the Alzheimer disease.
--- The Centre Democrats say they will not participate a 1997 state budget which meets leftwing demands for further tax increases.
